subject: faceting using a factor with repeated labels

messages.author: af62644095cc2666
messages.subject: faceting using a factor with repeated labels
parts:
I admit I am doing something weird: creating a factor with the same
label for different levels.

z<-factor(rep(1:3,50),labels=c("same","same","other"))

But the three distinct levels are still there, as I can check using
as.numeric. So when I facet using this factor I expect to get three
panels. But

x<-rnorm(150)
y<-rnorm(150)
qplot(y,x,facets=z~.)

produces a graph with only two panels, one labelled "same" and the
other labelled "other", whereas I had expected two panels labelled
"same" and one labelled "other".

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: faceting using a factor with repeated labels
parts:
Levels with duplicate labels are not a good idea. How can you know with
labels coresponds with a given level? It shouold be clear for a print()
of the dataset. If it requires as.numeric() then it's not a good idea.
Use two factors instead of one.

N <- 20
Dummy <- data.frame(x = rnorm(3 * N), y = rnorm(3 * N), Z = rep(1:3, N))
Dummy$F1 <- factor(ifelse(Dummy$Z > 2, "B", "A"))
Dummy$F2 <- factor(ifelse(Dummy$Z > 1, "C", "D"))
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(Dummy, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~F1 + F2)

HTH,

Thierry

>  y<-rnorm(150)
>  qplot(y,x,facets=z~.)
>
> produces a graph with only two panels, one labelled "same" and the
> other labelled "other", whereas I had expected two panels labelled
> "same" and one labelled "other".

# gives a warning message that it won't be ok to do this for
# much longer
z <- factor(rep(1:3, 50), labels = c("same", "same", "other"))

# note the space in the second "same "
z < -factor(rep(1:3, 50), labels = c("same", "same ", "other"))
qplot(rnorm(50), rnorm(50), facets = z~.)

HTH,

Philippe
